info.title: Docs API
info.description:
The HTTP API of the `docs` app, built with First and served under `/__first/api/v1` on its WordPress site.

Each request is dispatched to the WordPress REST route behind it, which enforces the app's access rules, field rules, validation and hooks; this API gives the requests and answers one plain shape.

A successful answer is JSON with the result under `data`; a list also has `cursor`, the next page's cursor or null. An error is an RFC 9457 problem document, `application/problem+json`, with `type`, `title`, `status`, `code` and `detail`, and `pointer` when one field is at fault.

Requests sign in as WordPress core accepts: the logged-in cookie with an `X-WP-Nonce` header, an application password, or a First Identity access token. Each operation says who may call it. A field the caller may not read is left out of rows, and can't be filtered or sorted on.

`first build` writes this document from the app's schema, with the typed client in `first/_generated/client/` and the app's WordPress Abilities; a component here has the name of the client's type for the same value.

get.description:
The docs rows the caller may read, one page at a time. `limit` is 50 unless given, and at most 100; `cursor` is null on the last page.

Access: Anyone may do this, signed in or not.

Rows that are not published are returned to editors and administrators only.

parameters.name: where
parameters.description: A filter, as JSON: a value or operators per field, with `AND`, `OR` and `NOT`. A filter on a field the caller may not read is refused.

parameters.name: orderBy
parameters.description: Fields to sort by, comma-separated; `-` before a field sorts it descending (`-createdAt,title`). Fields: `id`, `title`, `slug`, `content`, `description`, `parent`, `order`, `status`, `publishedAt`, `uid`.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Words to find, each at the start of a word, in the title, the content and every text field the caller may read. Only rows the caller may read are found, in the list's own order.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only rows with this status; shorthand for a filter on `status`.

parameters.name: with
parameters.description: What to load with each row, comma-separated or as a JSON object: `parent`, `children`. A relation holds only rows the caller may read.

post.description:
Creates one docs row and returns it.

Access: Users with the `editor` role or a higher one may do this.

requestBody.description: The new row's fields.

get.description:
One docs row.

Access: Anyone may do this, signed in or not.

Rows that are not published are returned to editors and administrators only.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The row's id, or `slug:<slug>` for the row with that slug.

parameters.name: with
parameters.description: What to load with each row, comma-separated or as a JSON object: `parent`, `children`. A relation holds only rows the caller may read.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: `md` answers with the row as Markdown (`text/markdown`) instead of JSON.

patch.description:
Changes the fields sent on one docs row and returns the row.

Access: Users with the `editor` role or a higher one may do this.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The row's id, or `slug:<slug>` for the row with that slug.

requestBody.description: The fields to change.

delete.description:
Deletes one docs row for good and returns the row as it was.

Access: Users with the `editor` role or a higher one may do this.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The row's id, or `slug:<slug>` for the row with that slug.

get.description:
Each saved version of the row, with its time and who saved it.

Access: Users with the `editor` role or a higher one may do this.

Needs the kind's update rule on the row; a row outside it is a 404.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The row's id, or `slug:<slug>` for the row with that slug.

get.description:
The row as this revision saved it.

Access: Users with the `editor` role or a higher one may do this.

Needs the kind's update rule on the row; a row outside it is a 404.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The row's id, or `slug:<slug>` for the row with that slug.

parameters.name: revision
parameters.description: The revision's id.

post.description:
Makes the revision the current row, as an update of the row.

Access: Users with the `editor` role or a higher one may do this.

Needs the kind's update rule on the row; a row outside it is a 404.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The row's id, or `slug:<slug>` for the row with that slug.

parameters.name: revision
parameters.description: The revision's id.

get.description:
The row as it would be once promoted, the fields that are staged, and who staged last. With `preview=<token>` it answers without signing in, through an anonymous visitor's field masks.

Access: Users with the `editor` role or a higher one may do this.

Needs the kind's update rule on the row; anyone else gets the 404 of a missing row, whether or not something is staged.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The row's id, or `slug:<slug>` for the row with that slug.

parameters.name: preview
parameters.description: A preview token from the preview route.

id.description: The revision that holds the staged version.

patch.description:
Saves the fields sent into the row's staged version. The live row stays as it is until the staged version is promoted. Checked as an update would be; no hook runs.

Access: Users with the `editor` role or a higher one may do this.

Needs the kind's update rule on the row; anyone else gets the 404 of a missing row, whether or not something is staged.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The row's id, or `slug:<slug>` for the row with that slug.

requestBody.description: The fields to stage.

id.description: The revision that holds the staged version.

delete.summary: Discard the staged version of docs
delete.description:
Ends the staged version. The live row is untouched; the discarded version stays in the row's revisions.

Access: Users with the `editor` role or a higher one may do this.

Needs the kind's update rule on the row; anyone else gets the 404 of a missing row, whether or not something is staged.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The row's id, or `slug:<slug>` for the row with that slug.

get.description:
The staged fields whose value differs from the live row, with both values, as the caller may read each side.

Access: Users with the `editor` role or a higher one may do this.

Needs the kind's update rule on the row; anyone else gets the 404 of a missing row, whether or not something is staged.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The row's id, or `slug:<slug>` for the row with that slug.

id.description: The revision that holds the staged version.

post.summary: Promote the staged version of docs
post.description:
Makes the staged version live, as an update of the row by the caller: its rules, hooks, unique checks and webhooks run. With `at` (a future time) the promote is scheduled instead, and `at: null` cancels a scheduled one; both answer with the staged version.

Access: Users with the `editor` role or a higher one may do this.

Needs the kind's update rule on the row; anyone else gets the 404 of a missing row, whether or not something is staged.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The row's id, or `slug:<slug>` for the row with that slug.

requestBody.description: Empty, or `at`.

200.description: The row after the promote, or the staged version when `at` was sent.

id.description: The revision that holds the staged version.

post.description:
A signed link to the staged version that works without signing in until it expires (an hour by default, a day at most) or the staged version is promoted or discarded.

Access: Users with the `editor` role or a higher one may do this.

Needs the kind's update rule on the row; anyone else gets the 404 of a missing row, whether or not something is staged.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The row's id, or `slug:<slug>` for the row with that slug.

requestBody.description: Empty, or `ttl` in seconds.

api.description: Reads the staged version without signing in.

url.description: The row's own page showing the staged version, when the theme renders it.

get.description:
Rows as sync records with their digests, in pages by id.

Access: Users with the `editor` role or a higher one may do this.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Only rows with an id above this one.

parameters.name: first
parameters.description: How many records to return, at most 100.

200.description: One page of records, and the id to pass as `after` for the next page, or null.

post.description:
Creates or updates one row from a content file, when the row still matches `expect`. A row that changed since answers 409 `sync_stale`.

Access: Users with the `editor` role or a higher one may do this.

requestBody.description: The record and the digest it expects.

expect.description: The digest the caller last saw, or `absent` for a row it believes does not exist.

200.description: The outcome: the row was updated, or was already as sent.

record.description: The record as stored, when the site normalized what was sent.

201.description: The outcome: the record created a row.

record.description: The record as stored, when the site normalized what was sent.

post.description:
Moves the row of a deleted content file to the trash, when the row still matches `expect`.

Access: Users with the `editor` role or a higher one may do this.

requestBody.description: The row's uid and the digest it expects.

expect.description: The digest the caller last saw, or `absent` for a row it believes does not exist.

post.description:
Converts a body between block markup, Markdown and HTML, as the site's own converters do. One item, or up to a batch under `records`.

Access: Users with the `editor` role or a higher one may do this.

requestBody.description: The text and the direction.

200.description: The converted text, or one result per item under `records`.

post.description:
Merges two versions of a body over their common base. One item, or up to a batch under `records`.

Access: Users with the `editor` role or a higher one may do this.

requestBody.description: The base and the two versions.

200.description: The merged text and whether it has conflicts, or one result per item under `records`.

patch.description:

Access: Users with the `admin` role or a higher one may do this.

requestBody.description: The fields to change.

get.description:
The user making the request, with their role; null when nobody is signed in.

Access: Anyone may do this, signed in or not.

Where First Identity signs users in (null without it), and whether guests are allowed.

Access: Anyone may do this, signed in or not.

post.description:
Creates a guest user and signs them in. A 404 when First Identity is not installed or guests are off.

Access: Anyone may do this, signed in or not.

delete.description:
Ends the First Identity session the request's access token belongs to. A cookie or application password signs out through WordPress instead, and is refused here.

Access: Any signed-in user may do this.

post.description:
Takes up to 20 reads, each with the `token` of the answer the caller last got, and answers each one as the caller, with every access rule and field rule applied. The typed client's `subscribe` calls it. An answer never says that something changed which the caller may not read.

Access: Anyone may do this, signed in or not.

requestBody.description: The subscribed reads.

kind.description: The kind, by the name the typed client uses.

args.description: The arguments of that call on the kind: `where`, `orderBy`, `limit`, `offset` or `cursor`, `with`, `search`, `locale`.

id.description: The row of a `get`; or give `args.where`.

token.description: What the previous answer to the same read returned. Opaque.

200.description: One result per read, in order, and the wait the client keeps between two requests.

items.description: `{ changed: true, token, data }` with the read's result as the caller reads it; `{ changed: false, token }` when what the caller holds is current; `{ error }` with the read's problem; `{ pending: true }` when the request ran out of time (ask again).

get.description:
Runs the kinds' `search` on every kind with a searchable field, as the caller. A kind the caller may not read is left out, and so is a `kinds` name that is not a searchable kind.

Access: Anyone may do this, signed in or not.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: The words to find.

parameters.name: kinds
parameters.description: Only these kinds, comma-separated: `docs`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Rows per kind: 10 unless given, and never more than 50.

200.description: The matching rows, by kind; a kind with none is absent.

get.description:
The app's kinds with the WordPress route behind each, their fields and access rules, its globals and its actions. `first sync` and `first doctor` read it.

Access: Anyone may do this, signed in or not.

runtime.description: The First runtime series and the WordPress, PHP, database and plugin versions under it.

kinds.description: Each kind by name: the WordPress route behind it, its fields, relations and access rules.

get.description:
The app's API as an OpenAPI 3.1 document: what `first build` wrote to `first/_generated/openapi.json`, with this site's address as its server.

Access: Anyone may do this, signed in or not.

title.description: The problem in a few words.

code.description: A stable name for the problem, such as `unauthenticated`, `forbidden`, `not_found`, `invalid_input`, `invalid_query`, `invalid_json`, `method_not_allowed`, `unique_violation` or `reference_violation`.

detail.description: What went wrong, for a person.

pointer.description: A JSON pointer to the field of the request at fault, when there is one.

children.description: Present when the request asks for it with `with`.
A filter on the related rows.

limit.name: limit
limit.description: How many rows to return: 50 unless given, and never more than 100.

cursor.name: cursor
cursor.description: The `cursor` of the previous page, to read the next one. It replaces `offset`.

Problem.description: An error, as an RFC 9457 problem document.

cookie.name: wordpress_logged_in_{hash}
cookie.description: WordPress's logged-in cookie, as a browser holds it after signing in. A request with it must also carry `X-WP-Nonce`.

nonce.name: X-WP-Nonce
nonce.description: A WordPress REST nonce (`wp_create_nonce('wp_rest')`) for the cookie's session.

applicationPassword.description: A WordPress user name and one of the user's application passwords.
